label: copy-phase input w (fed-back w from original position >= 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the fed-back input token is w (in_tok w covers 100% of activation mass; essentially no activity on any other token, and none in the original or delimiter phases). Equivalently, it fires on the step right after the model has output a w. Strength depends on where the w sat in the original sequence: weak or absent when w was original token 0-1 (recall_idx <= 2), strongest when w was late in the original (top examples have w at original positions 6-7). A w input that directly follows another w input in the copy phase gets a weaker activation than the first one. Does not depend on the token being output or on the surrounding tokens.

issues: The label and predicate hold up. All activation mass is in the copy phase (original and delimiter phases have 0 active steps). Input w accounts for 1.000 of the mass; the next most active input token, z, has 12 active steps out of about 199k. Activation does not vary with out_tok, prev_tok or prev2_tok (lift is about 1.2-2.5x for every value). Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.986, R 0.925, F1 0.954, mass recall 0.984.

One explanation claim is not supported: 'when a w input directly follows another w input, the second one activates more weakly'. At recall_idx 4, mass_recall/recall is 1.089 when the previous input was also w versus 1.047 when it was not (the repeat is slightly STRONGER). At recall_idx 6 it is 1.317 versus 1.365 (slightly weaker). Across all positions >= 3 it is 1.064 versus 1.063, so there is no systematic penalty for a repeated w. The anecdote in misses also goes both ways: 'i w w' gives 0.04 then 0.13, and '2 w w' gives 0.12 then 0.08. This sentence should be removed.
The position claim is correct. Mean activation rises steadily with recall_idx: mass/active is about 0.9e-5 at 3, 1.7e-5 at 4, 2.1e-5 at 5, 2.2e-5 at 6, 2.4e-5 at 7 and 2.6e-5 at 8.

The misses (4616 on test, 1.6% of mass) are almost all weak activations on w at recall_idx 2 (original position 1). Firing at recall_idx 2 depends partly on L: precision is 0.73 at L=4, 0.31 at L=5 and 0.17 at L>=7. Adding the case (recall_idx==2 & L<=4) raises test F1 only from 0.954 to 0.964, so this is a minor refinement, not a missing feature class.

The false positives (822, about 1.4% of predicted steps) are all w at recall_idx 3 (original position 2), where precision is 0.949. No token or history pattern stands out, so this looks like scattered noise near the low-position threshold.

Notation check: recall_idx is the output index, so the input at recall_idx r is original token r-1. 'recall_idx >= 3' therefore matches the label's 'original position >= 2'. The explanation's 'original token 0 or 1 (recall_idx <= 2)' is consistent with this.
